question: Refer to the exhibit. An engineer must configure port security on a Cisco MDS switch. The requirements are: the VSAN 4 port-security database must be activated and initiated despite conflicts with the existing configuration; static entries in the database must be added without database activation; the configuration must apply fabric wide; and any pending configuration lock must be released after the process is complete. Which command set accomplishes this task?
options: port-security activate vsan 4 / no port-security auto-learn vsan 4 / port-security distribute / abort
port-security activate vsan 4 / no port-security auto-learn vsan 4 / no port-security distribute / port-security commit vsan 4
port-security activate vsan 4 / port-security auto-learn vsan 4 / port-security distribute / port-security commit vsan 4
port-security activate vsan 4 force / no port-security auto-learn vsan 4 / port-security distribute / port-security commit vsan 4
theory: Each requirement maps to a specific MDS port-security command: activate vsan 4 force overrides conflicts with the current fabric state during activation; no port-security auto-learn vsan 4 ensures only explicitly configured static entries are used going forward (learning is off, so new logins are not silently added); port-security distribute turns on CFS-wide propagation; and port-security commit vsan 4 pushes the pending changes to every switch in the fabric AND releases the CFS lock - unlike abort, which would discard the changes instead of applying and releasing them. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 20 - Port Security, CFS Distribution Workflow)
